## Source-backed inputs

Packet C66-001-v4, SRC-0004 supplies the CE obstruction space, the convention W_f=(O(2)⊗γ^*O(-f))|_C, and deg(W_f)=4g+12-4f. Thus deg(W_4)=20 and deg(W_5)=16. The packet findings FND-0062 and FND-0063 record the corresponding fibrewise W_4 vanishing and W_5 degree-zero condition. These facts are rederived below before use. FND-0046 requires a scheme-structure comparison rather than geometric-point equality; FND-0047 requires avoiding an unjustified Proj(π_*L) construction when h^0 jumps. FND-0064 and FND-0087 delimit the ordered/unordered torsor statement. TASK-C66-M-001 has no dependency artifacts, so no prior attempt or review is used as a proof dependency.

## Proved steps

### 1. Evaluation bundles and the W_4 block

Since deg(W_4),deg(W_5)>2g-2=10, fibrewise Serre duality gives H^1(W_4)=H^1(W_5)=0. Hence π_*W_4 and π_*W_5 are vector bundles of ranks 15 and 11, commute with base change, and π_*(W_f|_Γ) has rank 6. Write φ_f for evaluation and φ=φ_4⊕φ_5.

The sequence 0→W_4(-Γ)→W_4→W_4|_Γ→0 shows that coker(φ_4)=R^1π_*W_4(-Γ). Its fibrewise Serre dual is H^0(ω⊗W_4^{-1}(Γ)); this line bundle has degree 10-20+6=-4, hence no section. Therefore φ_4 is surjective and I_6(φ_4)=O_S.

For the block-diagonal matrix φ, every nonzero 12-by-12 minor selects six columns from each block, so I_12(φ)=I_6(φ_4)I_6(φ_5)=I_6(φ_5). Thus Z_CE is exactly the maximal-minor scheme of φ_5. This proves the scheme-level form of the FND-0062 reduction.

### 2. Fibrewise Abel–Jacobi condition

For N=ω⊗W_5^{-1}(Γ), deg(N)=10-16+6=0. The same evaluation sequence gives coker(φ_5)=R^1π_*W_5(-Γ), whose geometric-fibre dual is H^0(N). A degree-zero line bundle on a smooth proper connected curve has a nonzero section only when its effective zero divisor has degree zero, hence precisely when it is trivial. Therefore evaluation fails geometrically exactly when N≅O_C, equivalently O_C(Γ)≅W_5⊗ω^{-1}. This independently verifies the fibrewise content of FND-0063, but does not yet identify the scheme structure.

### 3. Universal maximal-minor ideal on Pic^0

Let P=Pic^0(C/S), with identity section e, and choose a rigidified Poincaré bundle Poin on C×_S P. Let p:C×_S P→P and define L_univ=ω_{C_P/P}(Γ_P)⊗Poin^{-1}. It has relative degree 16, so R^1p_*L_univ=0; consequently p_*L_univ is a rank-11 vector bundle and its formation, and that of its evaluation map Φ:p_*L_univ→p_*(L_univ|_{Γ_P}), commutes with arbitrary base change. Put J=I_6(Φ).

From 0→ω⊗Poin^{-1}→L_univ→L_univ|_{Γ_P}→0 one gets coker(Φ)=R^1p_*(ω⊗Poin^{-1}). At a geometric point [Q] of P, its fibre is H^1(ω⊗Q^{-1}), dual to H^0(Q). Hence V(J) is supported set-theoretically on e(S), and J⊂I_e.

It remains to compare nilpotents. At a geometric point of e, ker(Φ)=H^0(ω), of dimension 6, and coker(Φ)=H^1(ω), of dimension 1. A tangent vector ξ∈T_{P/S,e}=H^1(O) is a first-order deformation of the trivial degree-zero bundle. A Čech lifting calculation shows that the induced first-order map ker(Φ)→coker(Φ) sends s∈H^0(ω) to ξ∪s∈H^1(ω). This is the Serre-duality pairing, so

H^1(O)→Hom(H^0(ω),H^1(ω))

is an isomorphism. In local bases where Φ has a 5-by-5 identity block modulo I_e, the linear terms of the maximal minors are precisely the components of this tangent map. They therefore generate I_e/I_e^2.

Let A be a local ring of P at a point of e and I=I_eA. The preceding calculation gives J+I^2=I. For the finite A-module M=I/J, multiplication by I satisfies IM=M. Since I lies in the maximal ideal of A, Nakayama's lemma gives M=0. Thus J=I locally along e. Away from e, Φ is surjective and both ideals are the unit ideal. Consequently I_6(Φ)=I_e globally as ideal sheaves. This closes the scheme-structure issue identified by FND-0046 without a transversality assumption.

### 4. Pullback to the CE family

The section a_N classifying N satisfies (id_C×a_N)^*Poin≅N⊗π^*Λ for some line bundle Λ on S. Therefore

(id_C×a_N)^*L_univ≅ω(Γ)⊗N^{-1}⊗π^*Λ^{-1}≅W_5⊗π^*Λ^{-1}.

Tensoring an evaluation map by a base line bundle does not change its maximal-minor ideal. Since R^1p_*L_univ=0, the W_5 evaluation matrix is the ordinary pullback of Φ even when a_N is not flat. Fitting ideals of a matrix commute with arbitrary scalar extension, so

I_6(φ_5)=a_N^*I_6(Φ)=a_N^*I_e.

The last ideal defines the scheme-theoretic inverse image a_N^{-1}(e(S)). Combining this with Step 1 proves Z_CE=a_N^{-1}(e(S)). The same calculation after any base change proves base-change stability. No assertion about underived pullback of p_*Poin is used, so Tor-independence is irrelevant.

### 5. Ordered and unordered incidence

For a balanced CE family before choosing markings, let Div^6_{C/S,rs} be the open locus of degree-six effective divisors with reduced support. The sum map Conf_6(C/S)→Div^6_{C/S,rs} is a finite étale S_6-torsor on stacks. Pulling it back along the Abel–Jacobi incidence O_C(D)≅W_5⊗ω^{-1} gives the corresponding torsor from the ordered CE failure locus to the unordered reduced-support incidence. This is an open part of the full incidence, not a closed locus. Over a nonreduced base the unreduced torsor is retained on both sides; after reduction the valid map is Z_ord,red→(Z_unord,rs)_red, in accordance with FND-0087.

## Computational hypotheses

None. No finite experiment is used.

## Gaps and scope

There is no gap in the stated scheme-theoretic theorem. It does not assert that the reduced-support incidence is nonempty on every fibre: Riemann–Roch proves only nonemptiness of the full degree-six Abel–Jacobi fibre, as emphasized by FND-0083. It also does not settle the h^0 stratification, components, dimensions, stabilizers, unbalanced closure, Tate support, or assembly into W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q); those are downstream subproblems.

## Failed routes

The blocked routes vcd-only-vanishing, undecorated-cgp-top-weight-graph-complex, point-count-without-degree-parity-separation, and forgetful-map-renaming-local-system-unknown are not used. They are cohomological routes unrelated to this relative determinantal/Picard comparison, and no new input is claimed for them.

claims.evidence: Block-minor factorization and the degree -4 vanishing for the W_4 obstruction.
claims.statement: The full balanced CE failure ideal I_12(φ) equals the W_5 maximal-minor ideal I_6(φ_5).

claims.evidence: Set-theoretic support, the Serre-duality first derivative, and the local Nakayama argument in Step 3.
claims.statement: The universal degree-16 evaluation maximal-minor ideal on Pic^0(C/S) is exactly the ideal of the identity section.

claims.evidence: Ordinary pullback of the universal evaluation matrix and compatibility of maximal minors with scalar extension.
claims.statement: Z_CE equals a_N^{-1}(e(S)) as closed subschemes and the equality commutes with arbitrary base change without Tor-independence.

claims.evidence: Free finite permutation action on ordered pairwise-distinct sections and compatible base change of the incidence.
claims.statement: Over the reduced-support open, ordering gives a finite étale S_6-torsor at stack level, with compatible reduction required over nonreduced bases.

summary: The balanced CE rank-failure scheme is proved scheme-theoretically, not merely set-theoretically, to be the degree-zero Abel–Jacobi identity pullback. The proof reduces the full evaluation determinant to the W_5 block, identifies the universal W_5 maximal-minor ideal on Pic^0 with the identity-section ideal using its Serre-duality first derivative and a local Nakayama argument, and then applies ordinary base change. No computational hypothesis or blocked cohomological route is used.
theorem_statement: Let π:C→S be a smooth proper family of geometrically connected genus-6 curves over a locally Noetherian characteristic-zero scheme, with six pairwise disjoint ordered sections and associated relative Cartier divisor Γ. Suppose the balanced tetragonal Casnati–Ekedahl bundle is split over S as W=W_4⊕W_5, where W_f=(O_{P(E^∨)}(2)⊗γ^*O_{P^1}(-f))|_C and the relative degrees of W_4 and W_5 are 20 and 16. Define the CE evaluation-failure scheme Z_CE by Fit_0(coker(π_*W→π_*(W|_Γ))). Put N=ω_{C/S}⊗W_5^{-1}(Γ), a relative degree-zero line bundle, and let a_N:S→Pic^0(C/S) classify N. Then Z_CE=a_N^{-1}(e(S)) as closed subschemes, where e is the identity section. This equality commutes with arbitrary base change and requires no transversality or Tor-independence hypothesis. On the universal ordered distinct configuration stack it is the pullback of the reduced-support Abel–Jacobi incidence, and the ordered-to-unordered map is a finite étale S_6-torsor; after reduction, both source and target must be reduced compatibly.
